caveats: Per-second with 5 minute minimum; powered-off Droplets STILL bill until destroyed; GPU Droplets have no CPU Droplet monthly cap. August 1 2026 price revision. Bundled CPU/RAM and local disks; transfer allowance included.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

Billing minimum conflict: docs (2026-08-25) say 60 s or $0.01 minimum; pricing-page FAQ says 5-minute minimum. Monthly: GPU Droplets have NO 672-h cap ('If you use your GPU Droplet for more than the standard 672-hour monthly limit, you will still be charged for the time you use'); embedded catalog monthly = hourly x 744. Newer customers may be charged mid-cycle when creating GPU Droplets.

Spot (public preview, Beta Service): no SLA, no support commitment, no service credits; 2-hour reclaim notice is best-effort ('may be reclaimed with less than two (2) hours' notice or ... with no notice'); boot and scratch disk data lost on reclaim; spot rate set independently of on-demand, locked at creation for the Droplet's life. Access 'limited to eligible accounts'.

fleet.verification: Payment method and tier prepayment/payment history.
fleet.tiers: GPU Droplet counts at tiers 1–5: 0/1/2/4/16. Prepayments $0/$50/$250/$1,000/$4,000; larger/custom quotas require request.
fleet.notes: GPU Droplet count is not physical GPU count for multi-GPU shapes. Tier 1 has no GPU Droplets. Immediate time describes prepaid tier changes only. AMD GPUs are gated: 'To use AMD GPUs, contact support to request access.' Multi-node GPU Droplets: 'To create multi-node GPU Droplets, you need to contact support to enable that functionality for your team.' Max 10 Droplets created at the same time (Control Panel/API). Tier 1 (new account, no prepay) = 0 GPU Droplets; one-time prepay of $50 unlocks Tier 2 = 1 GPU Droplet immediately; $4,000 prepay = Tier 5 = 16 GPU Droplets (count is Droplets, so 16 x 8-GPU = 128 GPUs). Also 'Request an increase' form (ticket) and automatic increases with payment history.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Snapshots are on-demand disk images of DigitalOcean Droplets and volumes saved to your account.
snapshot_auto.note: No state capture on power-off/idle; powering off just keeps the boot disk (and keeps billing). Optional scheduled Backups (daily/weekly) exist and for GPU Droplets 'include the boot disk but not the scratch disk' (https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/droplets/how-to/gpu/create/) - scheduled, not stop-triggered.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshots of GPU Droplets include the boot disk but not the scratch disk.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Disk only, no memory; live snapshot or powered-off snapshot via control panel/API/doctl. New GPU Droplets can boot from a snapshot: 'You can then use the snapshot as the base image to create additional GPU Droplets.' (https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/droplets/getting-started/recommended-gpu-setup/). Not incremental; each is a full disk image; attached volumes are not captured.

harness_api.note: Plain KVM GPU VMs managed by the Droplet API/doctl (create, power, snapshot); no first-party API to drive an agent harness inside the Droplet. DO's Gradient agent platform is a separate hosted-agent product, not an in-VM harness driver.

egress_allowlist.quote: Outbound firewall rules define what outgoing traffic to allow or deny, on which ports, and to which destinations. If no outbound rules are configured, no outbound traffic is permitted.
egress_allowlist.note: Cloud Firewalls (free, network-level, stateful, enforced before traffic reaches/leaves the Droplet). Destinations are IPs/CIDRs, Droplets, tags, load balancers, VPCs, K8s clusters + protocol/ports; no hostname/FQDN rules. Default-deny when attached. Applies to Droplets incl. GPU Droplets (no GPU exclusion listed in firewall limits).

egress_http_rules.quote: Firewall rules can allow or deny traffic by protocol, port range, and source or destination.
egress_http_rules.note: L3/L4 only; no HTTP method/path/header rules.

ingress_rules.quote: Inbound firewall rules define what traffic to allow or deny to the server, on which ports, and from which sources. If no inbound rules are configured, no incoming traffic is permitted.
ingress_rules.note: Cloud Firewall inbound rules by IP/CIDR/tag/Droplet/LB + port; VPC private networking; Droplets otherwise get a public IPv4 with all ports reachable. No managed preview URLs.

guest_firewall.quote: Firewalls can be host-based, which are configured on a per-server basis using services like iptables or UFW.
guest_firewall.note: GPU Droplets are full KVM VMs with root; iptables/UFW on the Droplet works (docs describe running UFW alongside Cloud Firewalls).

secret_proxy.note: Plain VM: secrets are whatever you put on the Droplet (user_data, files, env). No credential-injecting proxy documented.

volume_attach.quote: You can move a volume between compatible Droplets and GPU Droplets by detaching it from one Droplet and attaching it to another.
volume_attach.note: Volumes Block Storage (Ceph, 1 GiB-16 TiB, up to 15 per Droplet). A volume attaches to only one Droplet at a time.

volume_shared.quote: Concurrent access to shared datasets, model artifacts, and checkpoints across multiple GPU Droplets.
volume_shared.note: Network File Storage (managed NFSv4.1), read-write ('All access points provide read and write access; there is no read-only option'), up to 32 clients per share, same-region VPC; available in NYC2, AMS3, ATL1, RIC1, MKC1, MEM1 (overlaps H100/H200/MI300X GPU regions, not TOR1). Block volumes themselves are single-attach.
